q:
A registered representative wants to call a person who is on the federal do-not-call registry. Which of the following would permit the call?
I. The person has given the firm prior written consent
II. The rep has a personal relationship with the person
III. The person is an existing customer of the firm
IV. The call is placed at 8:30 am in the person’s local time
w: Wrong: this leaves out the existing-customer exception, which also removes the do-not-call restriction entirely.
Correct: written consent, a personal relationship, and existing-customer status are all exceptions; calling hours do not override the registry.
Wrong: the time of day does not create an exception, and this also omits the consent exception.
Wrong: a call at 8:30 am is within hours but does not permit calling someone on the registry.

q:
Which of the following are TRUE about verification of customer account information?
I. The first request goes out within 30 days of opening the account
II. After the customer reports a change, an updated record goes out within 30 days
III. Verification is repeated at least every 36 months
IV. In a joint account, only the first-named owner receives the notice
w: Wrong: this omits the requirement to send an updated record within 30 days of a customer’s change notice.
Wrong: joint accounts require the notice to go to each owner, so the fourth statement makes this choice incorrect.
Correct: the 30-day opening request, the 30-day post-change update, and the 36-month cycle are all required, and notices go to every joint owner.
Wrong: it leaves out the initial 30-day request and wrongly includes the first-named-owner-only statement.

q: All of the following are true about new account documentation EXCEPT:
o: The designated principal’s written approval becomes part of the permanent account record
The firm must maintain a record of new account forms
The customer and the registered representative must both sign the new account form
A principal may approve the account promptly after the first transaction
w: Wrong: this is true, since the written approval is kept as part of the permanent account record.
Wrong: this is true, because broker-dealers are required to maintain a record of new account forms.
Correct: only the designated principal approving the account signs the form, so requiring customer and rep signatures is false.
Wrong: this is true, since approval may come before or promptly after any transaction in the account.

q: A customer buys $20,000 of stock in a cash account on Monday in a regular way trade. Assuming no extension is requested, by which day must the customer pay under Regulation T?
w: Wrong: Tuesday is the regular way settlement date, not the Reg T payment deadline.
Wrong: Wednesday is only one business day after settlement, but Reg T allows two.
Wrong: Friday is three business days after settlement, which is past the deadline and when the sell-out occurs.
Correct: settlement is Tuesday and Reg T allows two further business days (S + 2), so payment is due Thursday.

q: A customer fails to pay for a cash account purchase by the Reg T deadline. All of the following are true EXCEPT:
o: The firm may ask its self-regulatory organization for more time
The position must be sold out on the morning of the third day if no extension is granted
The account is frozen for 90 days
The account must always be frozen, even when the payment shortage is $1,000 or less
w: Wrong: this is true, since the firm can request an extension from its SRO on the customer’s behalf.
Wrong: this is true, because without an extension the position is sold out on the morning of the third day.
Wrong: this is true, as a 90-day freeze is the normal consequence of late payment.
Correct: for shortages of $1,000 or less the firm has discretion to leave the account unfrozen, so “always” is false.

q: A cash account is frozen for free-riding and holds $3,000 in cash. The customer places an order to buy $5,000 of stock and promises to wire $2,000 later that day. What should the firm do?
o: Accept the order because the wire will arrive the same day
Reject the buy order because the full cash must already be in the account when it is placed
Accept the order only with a principal’s approval
Reject the order and also refuse any sell orders
w: Wrong: a frozen account may buy only with sufficient funds already on deposit, not funds that are promised.
Correct: frozen accounts may place buys only when cash covers the entire purchase at the time of the order.
Wrong: principal approval does not cure the lack of cash; the rule depends on funds already in the account.
Wrong: sell orders remain permitted in a frozen account, so refusing them is not required.

q:
Which of the following may be purchased on margin?
I. Exchange-traded fund shares
II. IPO shares on the tenth day after the effective date
III. Shares of a closed-end fund
IV. Mutual fund shares held for 45 days
w: Wrong: IPO shares cannot be bought on margin during the first 30 days after the effective date.
Correct: ETFs and closed-end funds are exchange-traded and eligible, while early IPO shares and mutual funds are not.
Wrong: mutual funds can never be purchased on margin; holding them 45 days only makes them usable as collateral.
Wrong: both of these are restricted, so this choice excludes the two eligible securities.

q: A customer wants to use mutual fund shares already owned in a margin account. Which statement is correct?
o: The shares may be purchased on margin after a 30-day holding period
The shares may serve as collateral for margin borrowing after being held at least 30 days
The shares may serve as collateral immediately upon deposit
Mutual fund shares may never be used as collateral
w: Wrong: mutual funds can never be purchased on margin, regardless of how long they are held.
Correct: although they cannot be bought on margin, mutual funds can be pledged as collateral after a 30-day hold.
Wrong: the 30-day minimum holding period must pass before mutual funds count as collateral.
Wrong: after 30 days they can be used as collateral, so a total prohibition is incorrect.

q: A customer buys $100,000 of municipal bonds in a margin account. Which statement about the initial margin is correct?
o: Regulation T requires a 50% deposit of $50,000
Municipal bonds cannot be purchased on margin
The Federal Reserve Board sets a 25% requirement
The requirement is set by the firm’s self-regulatory organization, such as FINRA, because municipal bonds are exempt from Reg T
w: Wrong: municipal securities are exempt from Regulation T, so its 50% rule does not apply to them.
Wrong: bonds are listed among securities eligible for margin purchase, and municipals are not prohibited.
Wrong: 25% is the FINRA long maintenance percentage, not a Federal Reserve initial requirement.
Correct: exempt securities such as municipal bonds and US government securities follow SRO margin requirements instead of Reg T.

q: A customer buys $40,000 of stock in a long margin account, depositing the Regulation T amount. The stock later falls to a market value of $26,000. What is the maintenance call?
w: Wrong: equity is $6,000 which is below the $6,500 required, so a call exists.
Wrong: this overstates the shortfall; the difference between required and actual equity is smaller than that.
Correct: the debit is $20,000 so equity is $6,000, the 25% requirement is $6,500, leaving a $500 call.
Wrong: $6,500 is the total maintenance requirement, not the shortfall the customer must deposit.

q: A firm charges broker call plus 0.50% on debit balances from $100,000 to $249,999, and broker call is 2.25%. A customer carries a $120,000 debit balance. What is the annual interest charge at that rate?
w: Wrong: $2,700 uses only the 2.25% broker call rate without adding the 0.50% spread.
Wrong: $4,200 would correspond to a 3.50% rate, which applies to a smaller debit balance tier.
Wrong: $5,100 would correspond to 4.25%, the rate on the smallest debit balances.
Correct: the rate is 2.25% + 0.50% = 2.75%, and 2.75% of $120,000 equals $3,300.

q:
Which of the following are TRUE about the margin agreement?
I. The hypothecation agreement permits the firm to re-pledge securities to a bank
II. Securities in a margin account must be held in street name
III. The credit agreement states the terms and interest on the borrowing
IV. The loan consent form is mandatory before the account may be opened
w: Correct: rehypothecation, street name registration, and credit terms are all true, while the loan consent form is technically optional.
Wrong: this omits the credit agreement, which does set the interest terms for the loan.
Wrong: this omits the hypothecation statement and wrongly treats the loan consent form as mandatory.
Wrong: the loan consent form is technically optional, so including it makes this choice incorrect.

q: A firm opens a margin account for a new customer in January. When must the firm provide the margin disclosure statement?
o: Only after the first margin call is issued
Before or at account opening, and annually
w: Wrong: the disclosure must be given at the start of the account, long before any margin call.
Correct: FINRA Rule 2264 requires delivery prior to or at opening, with the notice repeated every year.
Wrong: the margin disclosure repeat requirement is annual, not quarterly, so this schedule is incorrect.
Wrong: the notice must be renewed each year, so a one-time delivery is not enough.

q:
Which of the following are TRUE about opening an options account?
I. The options disclosure document is prepared by the OCC
II. It must be furnished at or before the time a registered options principal approves the account
III. The customer may not trade until the signed agreement is returned
IV. By signing the agreement the customer acknowledges position limits
w: Wrong: trading may begin on approval; the customer has 15 days to return the signed agreement.
Wrong: this leaves out the position limit acknowledgment the customer gives by signing the agreement.
Wrong: the OCC point is true, and the third statement is false because trading starts upon approval.
Correct: the OCC document, the timing before ROP approval, and the position limit acknowledgment are true, but trading can start before signing.

q: An options account was approved by a registered options principal ten days ago and the customer has not yet returned the signed options agreement. The customer wants to open a new long call position. What is the result?
o: The order is allowed because the 15-day period has not expired
The order is rejected because trading requires the signed agreement first
The order is allowed only to close existing positions
The order requires approval from a second principal
w: Correct: the customer may trade after approval and has 15 days from approval to return the signed agreement.
Wrong: the sequence permits trading upon approval before the agreement is returned within 15 days.
Wrong: the closing-only restriction applies only after 15 days pass without a signed agreement.
Wrong: no second principal is needed; one registered options principal’s written approval suffices.

q:
Which of the following trades are discretionary?
I. A customer asks to sell 300 shares of ABC and the rep sells 500 shares
II. A customer instructs the rep to buy 200 shares of DEF and the rep waits for a lower price before entering the order
III. A customer asks the rep to put $20,000 into bonds and the rep chooses the issues
IV. A rep recommends buying GHI and the customer approves before the order is entered
w: Correct: choosing the amount and choosing the asset are discretionary, while timing and customer-approved trades are not.
Wrong: timing and price are not discretionary, and a customer-approved recommendation is non-discretionary.
Wrong: waiting for a better price involves only time and price, which are not discretionary elements.
Wrong: a recommendation the customer approves leaves the final decision with the customer, so it is not discretionary.

q:
Which of the following are required for discretionary trading in a customer’s account?
I. Written power of attorney from the customer
II. Principal approval of the account before the first discretionary trade
III. Principal approval of each discretionary trade promptly after execution
IV. Signing the customer’s name to the power of attorney if the customer agrees and a signature is on file
w: Wrong: it omits the requirement that a principal approve each discretionary trade promptly after execution.
Wrong: it leaves out the written power of attorney and wrongly includes a prohibited signature practice.
Correct: written authority, pre-approval of the account, and prompt approval of each trade are required.
Wrong: signing for the customer is a prohibited signature of convenience even with the customer’s consent.

q: All of the following are true of UGMA and UTMA accounts EXCEPT:
o: Each account has one custodian and one minor beneficiary
Gifts to the account cannot be taken back
The minor may place trades if the custodian gives permission
w: Wrong: this is true, as a custodial account has only one custodian and one minor beneficiary.
Wrong: this statement is true, since gifts to a custodial account are irrevocable and cannot be reclaimed.
Correct: the custodian manages the account, and the minor cannot trade even with the custodian’s permission.
Wrong: this is true, because margin is not permitted in UGMA or UTMA accounts.

q: The custodian of a UTMA account dies before the minor reaches the age of majority. What happens to the account?
o: The courts name a successor custodian, typically a guardian or adult family member
The assets pass to the deceased custodian’s estate
The minor takes control of the account immediately
The minor’s eldest sibling becomes custodian automatically
w: Correct: courts appoint a successor custodian, usually the minor’s guardian or an adult family member.
Wrong: the assets belong to the minor, so they do not go to the custodian’s estate.
Wrong: control transfers to the minor only at the age of majority, not when a custodian dies.
Wrong: a successor custodian is named by the courts rather than appearing automatically by family rank.

q: A 17-year-old asks a registered representative to open an account in her own name, and her mother offers to be a joint owner with her. How should the representative respond?
o: Open a JTWROS account with the mother and the minor
Open a JTIC account with the mother and the minor
Refuse both and offer a UGMA or UTMA custodial account
Open an individual account with the mother’s signature as consent
w: Wrong: a minor cannot be part of a joint account of any kind.
Wrong: tenants in common is also a joint account, which a minor may not join.
Correct: a minor may only be a party to a UGMA or UTMA account, so the rep should offer that alternative.
Wrong: a minor cannot open an individual account, even with a parent’s signature.

q:
Which of the following are TRUE about trust accounts?
I. A revocable trust may be altered or cancelled by the trustor
II. An irrevocable trust cannot be changed without the agreement of the beneficiary
III. The trustee and the beneficiary can never be the same person
IV. The broker-dealer must be given a copy of the trust agreement
w: Wrong: this omits the requirement that the firm receive a copy of the trust agreement.
Correct: revocability, irrevocability limits, and the firm’s need for the agreement are accurate, while trustee and beneficiary may be the same person.
Wrong: the statement that trustee and beneficiary can never be the same is false, and this choice leaves out the revocable trust point.
Wrong: it includes the false statement that trustee and beneficiary can never be the same person and omits irrevocability.

q: Three different customers die. Customer 1 held a JTWROS account, customer 2 held an individual account with a transfer on death designation, and customer 3 held a share of a JTIC account. Which accounts avoid probate?
w: Wrong: the transfer on death designation also lets the individual account avoid probate.
Correct: JTWROS and an individual account with a TOD designation avoid probate, while JTIC assets are subject to it.
Wrong: JTIC assets are distributed through the deceased’s estate and are subject to probate.
Wrong: the JTIC account does not avoid probate, so not every account qualifies.

q:
Which of the following accounts require a statement at least MONTHLY?
I. A cash account holding only a money balance with no activity
II. An inactive account holding options
III. An active account holding penny stocks
IV. An active account holding only exchange-listed stocks
w: Wrong: money-balance-only accounts and listed-stock accounts need quarterly statements, not monthly ones.
Correct: any account holding options or penny stocks must receive monthly statements.
Wrong: an account holding only listed stocks is on the quarterly schedule.
Wrong: a money-balance-only account receives quarterly statements, so including it is incorrect.

q: A customer gives written instructions asking the firm to hold her mail for five months, citing security concerns. The firm agrees. Which of the following is NOT required of the firm?
o: Informing her in writing of alternatives such as website access or email notifications
Obtaining her confirmation that she received that information
Verifying at reasonable intervals that the hold instructions still apply
Requiring her to switch permanently to electronic delivery
w: Wrong: written notice of alternatives to monitor the account is a required step.
Wrong: the firm must have the customer confirm receipt of the alternatives information.
Wrong: verifying at reasonable intervals that the hold instructions still apply is a required firm step.
Correct: nothing requires a permanent switch to electronic delivery; the hold is permitted for a valid reason like safety.

q:
Which of the following are TRUE under Regulation S-P?
I. A privacy notice must be given before the customer enters an agreement to do business
II. The notice must be provided annually thereafter
III. A customer may opt out of sharing with non-affiliated parties
IV. A customer may opt out of sharing that is required in an IRS or anti-money laundering investigation
w: Correct: the notice is due before opening and annually, and customers may opt out of non-affiliate sharing but not legally required sharing.
Wrong: this omits the opt-out right for non-affiliated sharing, which the privacy notice must explain.
Wrong: sharing legally required, such as for the IRS, cannot be opted out, and the opening notice is omitted.
Wrong: customers cannot opt out of legally required sharing, so the fourth statement is false.
